Without anyone emerging as a viable replacement for Egbuka over the past two weeks, he should reclaim the No. 1 receiver role in Tampa Bay without much of a fight. Egbuka will be on the WR2/3 border for his first game back.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 9 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Kyle Dugger CIN Safety

The Bengals are surprisingly healthy headed into their date with the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. Dugger is the only one of their inactives who is out with an injury. The rest are healthy scratches.

item.title: Falcons EDGE James Pearce Jr. (back) is active for Week 9 against the Bengals.
item.description:
James Pearce ATL Defensive End

Pearce Jr. just finished serving his eight-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. A back issue then flared up in practice, but he’s good to go for his 2026 debut. Inactive for the Falcons are QB Andy Dalton, QB Jack Strand, WR Zachariach Branch, DB Billy Bowman, DB Robert Longerbeam, and DE Drake Jackson.

item.title: Falcons placed RB Brian Robinson (hamstring) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Brian Robinson ATL Running Back

The timing of the transaction is curious after Robinson missed the previous two games with the injury, potentially signaling a setback in his recovery. Either way, Robinson will now miss the coming four games, at minimum, leaving Bijan Robinson in a clear workhorse role in the immediate future.

item.title: Broncos activated WR Pat Bryant (ankle) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Pat Bryant DEN Wide Receiver

The young receiver will make his return to the active game-day roster after missing the minimum four games after injuring his ankle in Week 4. He returns to a passing attack with no clear direction or upside, with no receiver other than Courtland Sutton playing in a near every-down role of late. Perhaps he can carve out a featured role, but it is more likely this team simply doesn’t have viable weekly fantasy assets through the air.

item.title: 49ers activated WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Demarcus Robinson SF Wide Receiver

The veteran receiver returns to a decimated receiving corps, potentially in line to serve as the top receiver against the Raiders in Week 9. Fantasy managers in a bind could do much worse than taking a swing on Robinson considering the elite matchup and lack of viable depth, for a 49ers team with one of the week’s highest Vegas implied team totals on the board.

item.title: Vikings ruled out Jauan Jennings (calf) for Week 9 against the Bills.
item.description:
Jauan Jennings MIN Wide Receiver

The fantasy implications of Jennings’ absence are negligible, with the bigger boost to the passing offense being the absence of Kyler Murray, who is looking at a multi-game absence with a Grade 2 hamstring injury. Tai Felton appears to be in line for additional run as the team’s WR3, although he is not a recommended streaming option with both Jefferson and Jordan Addison healthy.

item.title: Vikings ruled out Kyler Murray (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Bills.
item.description:
Kyler Murray MIN Quarterback

Murray will likely be sidelined for multiple games after testing revealed a Grade 2 hamstring strain. Carson Wentz will draw the start under center while the team is reportedly exploring the trade market ahead of Tuesday’s deadline. The absence of Murray should benefit alpha wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who has struggled to develop chemistry with Murray this season.

item.title: Dion Dawkins (ribs) and Alec Anderson (ankle) are questionable for Week 9 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Dion Dawkins BUF Tackle

The Bills enter Week 9 with the entire left side of one the league’s top offensive lines questionable. Both players did not practice through Friday before drawing the questionable tag for Monday Night Football against the Vikings. We likely won’t know their respective statuses until inactives are released 90 minutes prior to first kick. Absences would be a detriment to the run game and could lead to increased emphasis on the short areas of the field through the air.

item.title: Bills ruled out Joshua Palmer (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Joshua Palmer BUF Wide Receiver

Palmer has been in and out of the lineup since injuring his hamstring in Week 4, managing only seven offensive snaps last week before succumbing to an aggravation. He will miss his second game of the season when the Bills take on the one-loss Vikings on Monday Night Football. Skylar Bell could find himself active for the third time in his rookie season, although DJ Moore, Keon Coleman, and Khalil Shakir are likely to dominate snaps and routes at the position.

item.title: Saints released RB Kendre Miller.
item.description:
Kendre Miller

The team brought back Audric Estime to their practice squad earlier in the week, releasing Miller Saturday. The moved comes after the veteran played 137 offensive snaps for a backfield missing its top option for most of the season. Miller had a 20-carry game for the Saints three short weeks ago and now finds himself without a home. Expect him to land on a practice squad in short order.

Source: Nick Underhill

item.title: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) “should be good to go” against the Browns in Week 9.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

The oft-injured Tyson hurt his hamstring in training camp and is yet to make his NFL debut. According to Schultz, he should be good to go Sunday against the Browns. A limited participant in practice throughout the week, it’s unclear how much Tyson might play in his first game. Eventually, though, he should settle in as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave. Tyson’s return also puts a damper on the fantasy prospects of Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Rams activated EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Myles Garrett

No surprise here as Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters Friday that Garrett is expected to play in Week 9 against the Commanders. The Rams are 4-4, but will finally have Garrett and Aaron Donald on the same defensive line. That could cause problems for opposing offensive lines, starting with Washington’s on Sunday.

Source: Rams

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Seahawks QB Drew Lock (elbow) has severe tendonitis in his elbow.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Pelissero reiterated that Lock looked good in practice and will start against the Cardinals in Week 9. Still, Lock has been dealing with this since earlier this season and at one point wasn’t able to throw because of it. Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald said earlier this week he didn’t know how much Lock will be able to throw. Despite his play in relief of Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) earlier this year, Lock isn’t a priority in 1QB leagues. Jalen Milroe could even be worth stashing in deeper formats given that Lock’s tendonitis could flare up at anytime.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: NFL reporter Aaron Wilson reports RB Dameon Pierce (hamstring) is drawing interest from multiple teams.
item.description:
Dameon Pierce

Pierce was released by the Eagles after agreeing to an injury settlement on Friday. He’s currently still dealing with what Wilson described as a “relatively minor” hamstring injury. Wilson lists the Dolphins, Jaguars, Panthers, Ravens, 49ers, Cardinals and Titans as teams that have contracted Pierce, who is rehabbing in Houston. Expected to be ready in 2-3 weeks, Pierce could catch on with another team soon, though it’s unlikely to be in a starting role.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Titans WR Calvin Ridley “could be had for a late-round pick.”
item.description:
Calvin Ridley TEN Wide Receiver

The Titans are listening on Ridley, who could be had for a late-round pick, according to Schefter. The Chiefs, Steelers and 49ers are the most likely teams to be in the market for a wide receiver ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero also reported that multiple wide receivers could be traded before the deadline and listed Ridley as a name to watch.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Titans aren’t interested in trading RB Tony Pollard.
item.description:
Tony Pollard TEN Running Back

A previous report from Albert Breer suggested the team might be willing to trade Pollard, who is in the last year of his contract, for a fourth-round pick. Schefter threw cold water on that theory, reporting Tennessee isn’t interested in trading the 29-year-old running back. Showing fresh legs in recent weeks, Pollard is a solid RB2 the rest of the way even on a struggling Titans offense.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Commanders “haven’t completely abandoned” the idea of acquiring WR Brandon Aiyuk.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk SF Wide Receiver

Aiyuk was rumored to end up in Washington all offseason and there seemingly could still be a fit there with Terry McLaurin out for the season. However, this report suggests the Commanders haven’t completely ruled it out rather than this being something they’re actively pursuing. Aiyuk met with 49ers brass Friday, though a resolution proved elusive. This saga is far from over.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts have told teams they’ve received an offer of a fourth-round pick for WR Josh Downs.
item.description:
Josh Downs IND Wide Receiver

The Colts’ original asking price for Downs, who has requested a trade, was a third-round pick. Indianapolis has told teams they already have an offer of a fourth-round pick for the 25-year-old receiver, who is in the last year of his rookie contract. Downs is probably one of the more likelier players to be traded ahead of the deadline. Teams have also called the Colts about Keenan Allen, though he’s unlikely to bring back a similar trade return given his age.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Chargers have no interest in trading EDGE Khalil Mack.
item.description:
Khalil Mack LAC Outside Linebacker

Despite the Chargers being 0-7, Los Angeles isn’t acting like it. Mack is 35, on an expiring contract and seeming could garner an early day-three pick in a trade. Still, the Chargers are content to keep Mack, who Schefter says won’t be going anywhere prior to the trade deadline.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Broncos checked on Trey McBride.
item.description:
Trey McBride ARI Tight End

To no one’s surprise, the Cardinals hung up the phone in record time. Even as a perennially rebuilding franchise, Arizona was never going to trade arguably the league’s best tight end in the middle of his prime. Schefter added that the Cardinals have “checked in around the league on tight ends.” Evan Engram has a measly 13 catches for 136 yards this year and Denver’s passing attack has taken a step back despite acquiring Jaylen Waddle in the offseason. Dallas Goedert is the biggest name believed to be available at tight end ahead of Tuesday’s deadline. On an expiring contract, he wouldn’t cost the Broncos much. Carolina tight end Ja’Tavion Sanders is likely on the trade block as well.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports the Jets have no desire or intention to trade RB Breece Hall.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

While the Jets traded young players for draft picks last season, don’t expect New York to do that again this year. A team source told Jones the Jets moving Hall is “very unlikely to happen.” Hall appears ready to return from a quad injury in Week 9 against the Chiefs, but is difficult to trust in fantasy with Braelon Allen potentially cutting into his workload after a strong showing in Hall’s absence in recent weeks.

Source: Jonathan Jones

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Vikings QB Kyler Murray has a Grade 2 hamstring strain.
item.description:
Kyler Murray MIN Quarterback

Previous reports said Murray was “week-to-week” with the injury. There’s no question the Vikings will monitor Murray’s health every week, but a Grade 2 hamstring strain typically leads to missing multiple games. With Carson Wentz set to start on Monday Night Football against the Bills in Week 9 and the Vikings monitoring outside QB options ahead of the trade deadline, Murray isn’t even guaranteed to be the starter again once he’s healthy.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lamar Jackson is out for 6-9 weeks with a fractured and dislocated thumb.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Per Rapoport, Jackson has already told his teammates he plans to return this season. While even the short end of that timeline would only have Jackson back in Week 15, it’s an optimistic turn of events for a quarterback who was previously expected to miss the rest of the season. At a nine-week return, Jackson would need Baltimore to make the playoffs to have a shot at returning this year. Jacoby Brissett will likely close out the fantasy season as Baltimore’s starting quarterback, but there’s a chance we get Jackson back for a final game or two in the regular season.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Patriots activated WR Mack Hollins (calf) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Mack Hollins NE Wide Receiver

Hollins misses the minimum four games with a calf injury and returns to a pass catching corps without A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson, while tight end Hunter Henry is also listed as questionable for Week 9. There is opportunity for him to lead the team in receiving with the bulk of the remaining healthy players largely operating in the short-to-intermediate areas of the field. Fantasy managers in a bid could do worse as a FLEX option against the Packers.

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts have told teams they aren’t trading QB Daniel Jones.
item.description:
Daniel Jones IND Quarterback

Despite ESPN’s Adam Schefter trying to will a Jones trade into existence by recreating Brian Windhorst memes, Pelissero reports the Colts have informed teams they aren’t trading the 29-year-old quarterback. Jones is set to start against the Cowboys in Week 9, but could find himself on the bench once the Colts are eliminated from playoff contention given the injury guarantees for next season in his contract.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Colts RB Jonathan Taylor “most likely” won’t be traded.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

An earlier report from the Athletic’s Jonathan Jones listed the Vikings and Giants as the favorites to trade for Taylor while the Seahawks, Packers and Broncos are still in the mix. Pelissero threw cold water on all of that by reporting no team has come close to offering what the Colts want for Taylor. Maybe that changes after Week 9, but if Taylor is stuck in Indianapolis, that’s probably the worst-case scenario for his rest-of-season fantasy value.

Source: Tom Peliserro

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts have received calls from multiple teams about trading for QB Daniel Jones.
item.description:
Daniel Jones IND Quarterback

Schefter passes along that the Ravens called the Colts about Jones before they acquired Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals. Otherwise, this report lacked specifics. According to league sources, multiple teams have called the Colts about trading for Jones, but he couldn’t name a team other than the Ravens. Schefter mentions the Vikings as a possibility, but while that suggestion makes sense given Minnesota’s need at quarterback and Jones’ history with the organization, it’s still purely speculation at this point. Jones is set to start against the Cowboys in Week 9, but isn’t on the fantasy radar outside of 2QB/superflex leagues.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Giants inquired about Ravens RB Justice Hill.
item.description:
Justice Hill BAL Running Back

Schefter reports that Hill rather than Derrick Henry was the running back the Giants called the Ravens about. While Henry is certainly the better back between the two, Schefter also reported that the Ravens won’t trade him. With Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doubtful and Tyrone Tracey on injured reserve, the Giants are looking for help in the backfield. Hill would help in that regard, but until a trade is consummated, he doesn’t have much standalone fantasy value behind Henry in Baltimore.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Ravens aren’t expected to trade RB Derrick Henry.
item.description:
Derrick Henry BAL Running Back

Citing league sources, Schefter says the Ravens recently informed Henry that they have no intention of trading him. While speculation about a trade is understandable given Baltimore’s injuries at the quarterback position, the Ravens are said to have never even considered it, according to Schefter. With the newly acquired Jacoby Brissett likely to be under center in Week 10 against the Chargers, Henry will be in the RB1 mix.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Chargers “still do not appear eager to sell players” ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
item.description:
Khalil Mack LAC Outside Linebacker

Fowler said he spoke to multiple executives around the league this week, and the general sentiment is that the Chargers are not interested in making any moves. Fowler wonders aloud whether Khalil Mack, who has generated “a lot of interest,” could be had for a fourth- or fifth-round pick. Mack, 35, certainly makes sense for contending teams. The 0-7 Chargers do not qualify as such.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Daniel Jones “maybe wants to” be traded away from the Colts.
item.description:
Daniel Jones IND Quarterback

Fowler says that multiple sources around the league, including multiple sources inside the Colts’ organization, believe Jones “should be trying to get out of Indy, or maybe wants to.” The Colts are entering a rebuild, with trade rumors swirling around multiple star players. Fowler closed the segment by hinting at the Vikings as a possible landing spot. Jones’ fantasy-scoring outlook might tick up a little bit were he to head back to Minnesota.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports that Jordan Elliott will work out for the Bears next week.
item.description:
Jordan Elliott

Elliott was released by the Titans a couple of weeks ago due to an “incident” at their facility. Schultz says that Titans coach Robert Saleh has been an “advocate” for Elliott despite the team releasing him. Should they bring him aboard, the Bears would further solidify their interior defensive line after recently acquiring Jeffery Simmons.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Brandon Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said talks between him and the 49ers are “to be continued.”
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk SF Wide Receiver

Aiyuk and Rosenhaus met with the 49ers’ “big bosses” today to discuss an amicable solution to their multi-year conflict. Aiyuk seeks reinstatement, but under league rules, he

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Kenny Gainwell (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
item.description:
Kenny Gainwell TB Running Back

Gainwell has been a little more involved in recent weeks, and coach Todd Bowles recently told reporters that they are getting closer to the 1A/1B usage that they envisioned when they signed him. Gainwell will again play sidekick to Bucky Irving this week.

Source: Tampa Bay Buccaneers

item.title: Tristan Wirfs (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
item.description:
Tristan Wirfs TB Tackle

The Buccaneers will have their starting left tackle on hand when they take on the Bears’ ascending defensive line in Week 9. Wirfs is one of the best offensive tackles in football. Having him on the field is always a plus for Baker Mayfield.

Source: Tampa Bay Buccaneers

item.title: George Pickens (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Colts.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Earlier today, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he is “hopeful” that Pickens will be available for this weekend’s game against the Colts. Pickens ended up being limited in practice all week and appears to be truly questionable to play. If active, he is a WR2 against a beatable Colts defense.

Source: Dallas Cowboys

item.title: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jets.
item.description:
Rashee Rice KC Wide Receiver

Rice posted a 7/53/1 receiving line against the Broncos last week. He got in a limited session on Wednesday before upgrading to full on Thursday. He seems to be recovering effectively from his summer knee procedure and in-season hamstring injury. Rice is a borderline WR1/2 for this weekend’s game against the Jets.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Travis Kelce (ankle) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jets.
item.description:
Travis Kelce KC Tight End

Kelce caught 5-of-7 targets for 67 yards, playing through the ankle injury last week against the Broncos, looking slightly hobbled. Kelce was limited to begin the week, but got in two full practices over the last two days. He remains firmly in the TE1 tier for Week 9 against the Jets.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
item.description:
Christian Darrisaw MIN Tackle

Darrisaw is now firmly on track to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills, who field a tough, talented defensive line. Having Darrisaw on the field will be helpful for pocket passer Carson Wentz.

Source: Minnesota Vikings

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that “the plan” is for Quenton Nelson to avoid injured reserve after undergoing a procedure to remove cartilage fragments from his knee.
item.description:
Quenton Nelson SEA Guard

If the Seahawks were to place Nelson on short-term injured reserve, he would be required to miss at least four games. The Seahawks face the Cardinals this week, the Raiders next and then go on bye. Nelson could have a chance to play in Week 12 against the 49ers. His availability that week will likely just come down to how the recovery is going. His loss is unfortunate.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Michael Wilson (NIR-rest/ribs) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Michael Wilson ARI Wide Receiver

Wilson caught 8-of-15 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 8 win over the Cowboys while playing through a pair of broken ribs. The Cardinals kept him limited all week. He should be good to go for WR2 duties against the Seahawks’ elite defense this week.

Source: Arizona Cardinals

item.title: Commanders ruled out Treylon Burks (foot) for Week 9 against the Rams.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

The Commanders’ wide receiver corps continues to lose players. Burks and Dyami Brown (calf) will both be sidelined this weekend, leaving Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams and Chig Okonkwo to operate as the top pass catchers.

Source: Nicki Jhabvala

item.title: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Talanoa Hufanga DEN Safety

The Broncos’ talented safety might need another week to get his ankle healthy. Hufanga only logged two limited practice sessions this week. He has been sidelined since mid-October.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Pat Bryant (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Pat Bryant DEN Wide Receiver

Bryant is expected to be activated from injured reserve by Saturday, but the team has officially listed him as questionable. He makes for a boom-bust FLEX in his first game back. The Broncos’ passing offense has struggled this season. Perhaps Bryant’s return lifts it up.

Source: Chris Tomasson

item.title: Dion Dawkins (ribs) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Dion Dawkins BUF Tackle

Dawkins and starting LG Alec Anderson (ankle) have now missed two practices this week. This is concerning. The Bills face the Vikings’ elite, blitz-based defense in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game. Hopefully, the extra day off helps them return in time.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Keon Coleman (shoulder) was limited on Friday.
item.description:
Keon Coleman BUF Wide Receiver

Coleman’s fantasy-scoring outlook has been hurt by his teammate’s improving health. At this point, Coleman is more so a single-game DFS FLEX rather than a starter in 12-team re-draft formats. He should be good to go for Week 9’s Monday Night Football game though.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited on Friday.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

The Bills are managing Moore’s AC joint sprain fairly well. He should be expected to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Vikings. Although it is a tough matchup, Moore remains the WR2 tier in this week’s final game.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Dalton Kincaid (chest) practiced in full on Friday.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Kincaid remained limited in all three practices last week, so today’s return to full participation is great to see. The Vikings’ blitz-based defense often requires tight ends to stay in line to block, which could hurt Kincaid’s route volume. Regardless, he is too talented to be removed from the TE1 ranks.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: David Njoku (fibula) is doubtful to play in Week 9 against the Texans.
item.description:
David Njoku LAC Tight End

Njoku was limited all week, though he apparently is not ready to return from injured reserve. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. The Chargers will likely employ a three-player rotation whenever he returns.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Texans ruled out Reed Blankenship (consussion/hand) for Week 9 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Reed Blankenship HOU Safety

The Texans will be without Blankenship this week, but they get Jalen Pitre (shoulder) back. The Texans’ defense has underperformed this year, as has the Chargers’ offense. Perhaps one of the units can facilitate a get-right outing for the other.

Source: Houston Texans

item.title: 49ers ruled out Christian Kirk (knee) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

At this point, Kirk probably does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues. He returned from his lengthy calf injury only to injure his knee. It’s a tough break for the veteran wide receiver.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Demarcus Robinson (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Demarcus Robinson SF Wide Receiver

If Robinson can make his return from injured reserve with Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (knee) sidelined, Robinson could end up returning WR3 value against the Raiders this week. Wide receiver-needy fantasy managers should add him now.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: 49ers ruled out Deebo Samuel (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Deebo Samuel SF Wide Receiver

Samuel, Mike Evans (Achilles) and Christian Kirk (knee) are all sidelined, potentially leaving Demarcus Robinson (ankle) as a featured receiver if he can play. Samuel can continue to be stashed on benches in 12-team leagues, though his return timeline remains somewhat opaque.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: 49ers ruled out Mike Evans (Achilles) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans is dealing with tendinitis in his Achilles tendon that initially cropped up in Week 6. When speaking with the media earlier this week, general manager John Lynch said the team hopes to get Evans back in the “coming weeks,” which means he should tentatively be considered questionable to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Nick Bosa (calf/knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Nick Bosa SF Defensive Lineman

Bosa strained his calf while going through his pre-practice warm-up routine before Week 3’s Thursday practice, and has not played since. He has also dealt with knee tendinitis. Bosa is finally cleared to return following the 49ers’ Week 8 bye.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Christian McCaffrey SF Running Back

McCaffrey injured his hamstring in Week 7. The 49ers were on bye in Week 8, giving him extra time to rest. McCaffrey then sat out on Wednesday before practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday. He should be in fantasy football lineups this week, facing a soft Raiders run defense, but Kaelon Black could mix in for 8-10 touches, potentially warranting FLEX consideration.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Rams ruled out Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) for Week 9 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson was set to make his return from injured reserve, having rehabilitated his early-season ankle injury. Unfortunately, he strained his hamstring in practice today and has now been ruled out. With Colby Parkinson (ribs) questionable, Tyler Higbee sneaks back into the TE1 conversation.

Source: Dan Graziano

item.title: Drew Lock (elbow) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Lock has dealt with an injury in his throwing-arm elbow for multiple weeks. He was limited at each Week 9 practice, but told reporters that he was feeling good late on Wednesday. It is tough to say whether this will impact him on game day, but he warrants QB2 treatment against the Cardinals’ soft defense.

Source: John P. Boyle

item.title: Seahawks ruled out Rashid Shaheed (knee) for Week 9 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

The Seahawks will again be without their speedy, underused wide receiver. Fortunately, Tory Horton (hand) was removed from the injury report and will play this week. He will catch passes thrown by Drew Lock (elbow).

Source: John P. Boyle

item.title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quenton Nelson (knee) will have a minor procedure and is week-to-week.
item.description:
Quenton Nelson SEA Guard

Apparently, Nelson was dealing with this knee issue when Seattle acquired for him, and he recently “aggravated it to some degree.” FOX 59’s Mike Chappell notes that Nelson was never listed on the Colts’ injury report this season. This is a bummer for the Seahawks, who acquired Nelson as a win-now move. Nelson will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals, and the Seahawks also ruled out LT Charles Cross (ankle), DT Leonard Williams (stinger) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle).

Source: Mike Chappell

item.title: Mason Taylor (back) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Mason Taylor NYJ Tight End

Taylor’s contributions are far too volatile for him to be trusted in 12-team formats, but his presence hurts rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq’s fantasy-scoring outlook. Taylor does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Sione Vaki (ankle) is questionable for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Sione Vaki DET Running Back

Vaki and Lions RB3 Jacob Saylors (neck) are both questionable. Vaki did not practice on Friday, having apparently suffered a new injury. Saylors was limited all week. Jahmyr Gibbs should handle his normal, sizable workload.

Source: Detroit Lions

item.title: Lions ruled out Cade Mays (ankle) for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Cade Mays DET Center

Brutal. Mays returned from injured reserve in Week 7 due to a preseason wrist injury. He injured his ankle in Week 8. The Lions ruled out S Kerby Joseph (knee) and CB D.J. Reed (hip), yet S Brian Branch (concussion) will play.

Source: Detroit Lions

item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Amon-Ra St. Brown DET Wide Receiver

St. Brown rarely misses games due to injuries. Fantasy managers should remain optimistic about his availability. The Lions’ No. 1 wide receiver remained limited all week. Although it might hurt to take hits, we expect St. Brown to suit up this weekend. Regardless, keeping it locked to Rotoworld is a must. Updates will be provided as they roll in.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Jaylen Wright (quad) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Lions.
item.description:
Jaylen Wright MIA Running Back

Wright and Dolphins RB3 Kaytron Allen (quad) are both questionable in this one, though Allen upgraded to full participation on Friday while Wright remained limited. Wright is barely worthy of stashing in 12-team leagues.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Panthers ruled out Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Jaelan Phillips CAR Outside Linebacker

Phillips did not practice at all this week, after sitting out the Panthers’ last two games. Losing a key edge rusher will make things harder for the Panthers’ defense. Bo Nix should have decently comfortable pockets, though.

Source: Alex Zietlow

item.title: Malik Nabers (knee) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

The Giants have smartly limited Nabers’ practice participation levels at times this season, allowing him to play very well while returning from last year’s season-ending knee injury. Nabers belongs in fantasy football lineups in this divisional showdown, as usual.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is doubtful to play in Week 9 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

Giants coach John Harbaugh told reporters earlier this week that Skattebo is day-to-day. Unfortunately, Skattebo only got in one limited session on Friday. Fantasy managers should expect Devin Singletary to get the start this week. He can be treated as a volume-based FLEX.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Eagles ruled out Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) for Week 9 against the Giants.
item.description:
Jihaad Campbell PHI Linebacker

Campbell will now miss another game, beset by upper-leg injuries. The Eagles also ruled out DBs Michael Carter (abdomen) and Jonathan Jones (hamstring). The Eagles still have talented players available, but the defense is a little banged up.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: Jake Elliott (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Giants.
item.description:
Jake Elliott PHI Kicker

The Eagles’ kicker practiced in full today, which was good to see. Given the state of the Eagles’ offense, he may not have many field goal attempts this week, though. Kickers tend to benefit from playing on teams with stellar offenses. The Eagles no longer have one.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: Eagles ruled out Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 9 against the Giants.
item.description:
Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will both miss this weekend’s game, before taking the week off next week as well. The Eagles go on bye in Week 10. Hopefully, the added rest will allow Wicks to be healthy down the stretch.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Giants.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley will again play through his hamstring and back injuries. Touchdowns have helped offset Barkley’s moderate yardage totals, and the offense will now be led by Joe Milton. Barkley’s role and talent keep him in the high-end RB2 tier, though an apex outcome is perhaps unlikely, given the state of the Eagles’ offense.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Giants.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

As expected, Smith will miss another week after not being able to practice due to his ankle troubles. The 27-year-old wideout could be an option after the Week 10 bye, but nothing is certain. The Eagles’ passing attack should be completely avoided for their divisional showdown with New York.

Derrick Brown CAR Defensive Tackle

The Panthers are “not actively looking to move” Brown, but Breer says they have considered it. The Dolphins have told teams they are not interested in trading away Zach Sieler.

item.description:
Jauan Jennings MIN Wide Receiver

Jennings was limited yesterday, which could mean he injured his calf during the Vikings’ Thursday practice. If this is the case, he is probably unlikely to suit up for his team’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills.

Source: Alec Lewis

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Josh Downs “leads the wide receiver market” ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
item.description:
Josh Downs IND Wide Receiver

Downs’ 2026 season has fallen short of expectations, but perhaps he has a chance to rebound. Breer believes acquiring Downs would “probably” cost a fourth-round pick. He is “one of a number of receivers on the market” at the moment, with the Chiefs and Steelers among the teams looking for help at the position. Breer adds that the 49ers are “open” to adding a wide receiver as well, but with their positional health improving, San Francisco is “less desperate than they were a couple of weeks ago.” The Steelers’ wide receiver corps might be too muddled for Downs to meaningfully increase his productivity, but landing in Kansas City or San Francisco would likely be good for him.

Source: Sports Illustrated

item.title: Emeka Egbuka (foot) is listed as questionable for Week 9 against the Bears.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka was able to get in another full practice Friday after getting the same Thursday, so it seems like he’s on the right side of the questionable tag, even with coach Todd Bowles suggesting he’ll be a game-time decision. The 24-year-old wideout is on the WR2/WR3 range for the Sunday Night Football showdown against Chicago if he is able to go.

Source: Rick Stroud

item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

Source: Cleveland Browns

item.title: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was ruled out for Week 9 against the Colts.
item.description:
KaVontae Turpin DAL Wide Receiver

This will be a third-straight missed game for Turpin as he battles his rib issue. The 30-year-old has just seven targets on the season, but will again be missed by Dallas in the return game. Malachi Lawrence has also been ruled out by the Cowboys due to his ankle injury.

Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the Jaguars “have been less inclined” to trade away Brian Thomas.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

Breer and NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe put out similar reports today, indicating that the Jaguars are now hesitant to trade away Thomas. Per Breer, Thomas is not the best fit for coach Liam Coen’s scheme, but he “brings a downfield element that’s really important in keeping defenses honest against the run, and opening things up underneath for Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington.” Wolfe echoed Breer’s downfield sentiment and added that when the Jaguars traded away Tyson Campbell last year, it had a negative impact on the locker room — and Jaguars brass has “learned from it.” Thomas and Travis Hunter are reportedly close friends, and Thomas is liked in the locker room. It sounds like the formerly productive wide receiver might be staying put. Breer lists the Chiefs and Steelers, and the 49ers to a lesser degree, as the teams known to be seeking wide receiver help.

Source: Sports Illustrated

item.title: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) returned to practice Friday.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

The Bears are calling the tailback questionable for Week 9 against the Buccaneers. It’s the first time that Monangai has been able to practice picking up the injury a month ago against the Jets. It seems extremely unlikely that the 24-year-old will be able to play against Tampa Bay on Sunday night, but he appears to be on track to return after the Week 10 bye for the final stretch. Malik Muhammed and Tyrique Stevenson are also questionable for the Sunday Night showdown.

Source: Brad Biggs

Per Breer, the Colts either want a first-round pick or a draft pick package similar to what the Panthers received for Christian McCaffrey in 2023. The 49ers handed over 2023 second-, third- and fourth-round picks, and a 2024 fifth-rounder to acquire him. None of the three suitors have met either asking price yet. That said, the Giants have reportedly offered enough for Breer to label them “a serious suitor.” Stay tuned.

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

Parkinson sat out on Wednesday and Thursday. His Friday participation level has not yet been released, but he is probably on the wrong side of questionable at this time. Parkinson does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues, especially with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) expected to play.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Jordan Whittington (back) is questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Jordan Whittington

item.description:
Kelvin Banks NO Tackle

Source: Kat Terrell

item.title: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters that Terrance Ferguson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson will be able to play for the first time since he suffered his medial ankle sprain in Week 3. The second-year tight end offers some volatility, but there’s no denying that there’s upside in his profile. Just don’t be shocked if it isn’t on full display just yet in Week 9.

CJ Donaldson NO Running Back

Donaldson wasn’t able to practice again Friday, and the 22-year-old tailback won’t be available for the Week 9 skirmish against Cleveland. item.title: Deshaun Watson (concussion) will not start in Week 9 against the Saints.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

Head coach Todd Monken said Watson will be questionable for Sunday’s game, but has already said Shedeur Sanders will make his first start of the season. Watson missed Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday, although he has yet to clear concussion protocol. The decision to start Sanders likely stems from him working with the first-team offense during the week and the unlikelihood of Watson clearing protocol in time for Sunday’s game.

Source: Andrew Siciliano

item.title: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young (ankle) will play in Week 9 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Bryce Young CAR Quarterback

Young never really felt like he was at risk of missing this week. Despite dealing with an ankle injury, the Panthers’ QB1 was listed as a full participant in practice throughout the week and will be good to go despite what appears to be a minor ankle injury. Young draws a tough Week 9 matchup at home against the Broncos and has thrown two touchdowns and three interceptions in his last two games, and has completed below 60 percent of his passes in his last three outings. He’ll be a risky QB2 this week.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Packers.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Brown was unable to practice again Friday, and the 29-year-old will not be able to roll against the Green Bay secondary. It’s a second-consecutive missed game for Brown, who has played in just three games since his blockbuster deal to the Patriots prior to the season. DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will be Drake Maye’s top wideout targets for the game against Green Bay. Not ideal.

Source: James Palmer

item.title: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight (concussion) will not play in Week 9 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Zonovan Knight ARI Running Back

LaFleur also ruled out OL Jon Gaines II (ankle) and OT Jayden Williams (knee). Knight has been a DNP all week after suffering a concussion in Week 8’s win over the Cowboys and will officially be sidelined for Week 9. His absence, along with Jeremiyah Love’s (ankle) could create a bell cow role for Tyler Allgeier, who totaled 191 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns in last week’s win, while fourth-year vet Evan Hull could also work into the mix. Allgeier’s volume alone will put him in the RB2 conversation this week despite the tough matchup.

Source: Josh Weinfuss

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Myles Garrett (knee) “is on track to be activated ahead of Sunday vs. the Commanders.”
item.description:
Myles Garrett

Garrett has practiced all week and will likely be activated in the next 24 to 48 hours. The star pass-rusher who was acquired by the Rams in a blockbuster trade this offseason played in just one game for the Rams this season and did not record a tackle. Now, after undergoing knee surgery to correct a nagging injury, Garrett is all but set to return against the Commanders after missing seven straight games. His return will provide a much-needed boost to a Rams defense that ranks near the bottom of the league in sacks (12) through the first half of the season.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Malik Nabers (knee) returned to practice on Friday.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Nabers was a surprise DNP with a knee injury on Thursday, but said after practice that he expected to play. His return to the field on Friday suggests he will be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Eagles, but we will still check in with a final status when the Giants announce player designations for the weekend. Assuming he is good to go, Nabers should be treated as a normal must-start receiver against a down-bad Eagles team.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: DJ Turner (heel) will play in the Bengals’ Week 9 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
DJ Turner CIN Cornerback

After being upgraded to a full participant in Thursday’s practice, Turner was officially removed from the injury report on Friday, meaning he will be good to go for Sunday’s international tilt against the Falcons. Turner has allowed 16 receptions for 133 yards and one touchdown on 26 targets this season, per PFF, earning a coverage grade of 72.9.

Source: Cincinnati Bengals

item.title: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

This comes a day after Hall said he expects to play, so this news isn’t all too surprising. Hall’s return could somewhat complicate the Jets’ backfield situation on Sunday, however, as Braelon Allen has played well in Hall’s absence, making a strong case for more touches even when Hall is healthy. Glenn declined to get into how he plans to divvy up his running backs’ touches next week, saying “both guys will play,” when asked about his plans. This was already shaping up to be a tough fantasy matchup on the road against the Chiefs, but a potential backfield split would only further complicate matters. Until we see how things shake out, both Hall and Allen should be viewed as mid-to-low-end RB2s.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said Kadyn Proctor cleared concussion protocol and will play in Week 9 against the Lions.
item.description:
Kadyn Proctor MIA Offensive Lineman

Proctor missed last week’s game against the Patriots with a brain injury, but will be back in his normal left guard position for this week’s game against the Lions. In six games this season, Proctor has appeared on more than 350 offensive snaps, earning a PFF grade of 64.8 while allowing one sack and 13 pressures.

Source: Barry Jackson

item.title: The Ravens and Cardinals finalized a trade on Friday that sends Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore.
item.description:
Jacoby Brissett BAL Quarterback

We already knew this deal would be done, but the two sides made things official on Friday. The Ravens will receive Brissett, along with a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Cardinals in exchange for a 2027 4th-round pick and a 2028 7th-round pick. Brissett will immediately step into a starting role for the Ravens when they face the Chargers in Week 10 and should provide an immediate upgrade over Joe Fagnano, who struggled mightily in his first career start against the Jaguars.

item.title: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Garrett Wilson (concussion) will not play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Garrett Wilson NYJ Wide Receiver

Wilson has not practiced this week and has now been ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Chiefs. Wilson has caught 43 passes for 527 yards and three touchdowns this season and saw 12 targets in last week’s loss to the Raiders. His absence means both Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper should see expanded roles, but both players will be hard to trust as anything more than WR3s against a stout Chiefs defense. In addition to Wilson, the Jets also ruled out LB Trevin Wallace (groin) for Week 9.

Source: New York Jets

item.title: TreVeyon Henderson released a statement saying that he was dealing with an “unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days.”
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

This certainly sounds like a scary situation for Henderson, whose absence has been the subject of speculation for nearly two weeks. Henderson said that the results of “comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, but he continues to work with specialists and physical therapists. Henderson said these issues have affected his “strength, coordination, and some of [his] physical functions,” while adding that he is working to return to full health. While we don’t want to speculate too much, it doesn’t sound like Henderson will be back anytime soon. Hopefully we will get more clarity on his situation soon, but our thoughts are with him and his continued recovery.

Source: TreVeyon Henderson

item.title: Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he is “hopeful” George Pickens (hamstring) will play in Week 9 against the Colts.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Pickens has been limited in each of the Cowboys’ first two practices to start the week, which would seem to be a good sign for his Week 9 availability. We’ll get a better sense of where things stand when the Cowboys release their final injury report on Friday and give Pickens a designation heading into the weekend, but Schottenheimer’s optimism is a good sign. Owner Jerry Jones advocated for Pickens getting the ball more this week after Week 8’s loss to the Cardinals, so if he is active, the star receiver could be primed for a bit of a squeaky wheel game in a plus matchup against the Colts.

Source: Tommy Yarrish

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Deshaun Watson (concussion) is “unlikely to start” in Week 9 against the Saints.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

Watson has not practiced this week due to concussion symptoms he has been dealing with since Week 8’s loss to the Steelers. Unless he surprisingly clears concussion protocol this week, Watson will miss Week 9, paving the way for Shedeur Sanders to make his first start of the season. We will have official word on Watson’s status in a few hours, but at this point, it would be surprising if he does start.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Brandon Aiyuk owes the 49ers “roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture,” which could delay his return.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk SF Wide Receiver

Pelissero calls this a “potential complication in [Aiyuk’s] efforts to secure his release by reporting to the facility Friday.” While it’s possible both sides reach a deal for Aiyuk to pay back that money, which would make this a non-issue, Pelissero said this could also end up going to arbitration, which may delay things. Aiyuk is scheduled to report to the 49ers’ facilities today, so we could have our answer in the next few hours about when this situation is resolved and Aiyuk has been granted his release. Aiyuk recently hired Drew Rosenhaus with the hopes of being reinstated into the league and with a new team soon. The 28-year-old last played in 2024.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: James Pearce is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Bengals.
item.description:
James Pearce ATL Defensive End

Pearce’s status is related to a back injury that apparently flared up in Friday’s practice, per head coach Kevin Stefanski. Pearce was a full participant in practice, and teams said he will operate on a pitch count, so it seems highly unlikely he will be scratched on game day. In addition to Pearce, the Falcons also listed LB Yasir Abdullah (hamstring), WR Beaux Collins (hip), LB Divine Deablo (forearm), and OT Cameron Williams (ankle) as questionable for Week 9.

item.title: Brian Robinson (hamstring) is questionable for the Falcons’ Week 9 game against the Bengals.
item.description:
Brian Robinson ATL Running Back

Robinson was briefly listed as questionable only for head coach Kevin Stefanski to rule him out shortly after the initial report. Robinson was limited in practice throughout the week, but the Falcons are opting to play it safe, likely hoping another week on the sidelines will lower the chances of re-injury. Rookie WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring) has also been ruled out for the game after picking up an injury in last week’s loss to the Buccaneers.

Source: Tori McElhaney

item.title: Mark Andrews caught both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description:
Mark Andrews BAL Tight End

Andrews, somewhat disgustingly, led the team in receiving with a modest 19 yards on a night undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano threw for only 60 yards in his first career start. It remains difficult to start the veteran tight end, who has made more mental mistakes this season than he has receptions.

item.title: Zay Flowers caught 3-of-6 targets for six yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding 17 yards on three carries.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did what he could to overcome undrafted free agent rookie Joe Fagnano under center, routinely putting Flowers in Motion across the formation to generate some level of misdirection for an offense with zero ability to attack downfield. That included three rush attempts and a completion thrown by running back Derrick Henry, but it wasn’t enough to salvage a usable fantasy week for the electric receiver. Fantasy managers can rest easy knowing help is on the way in the form of veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who was signed earlier in the week and will likely make his team debut when the Ravens take on the Chargers in Week 10. Flowers will return to upside WR2 range with the change at quarterback.

item.title: Derrick Henry rushed 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description:
Derrick Henry BAL Running Back

Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did everything in his power to overcome an undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in his first professional start, going so far as to call numerous direct snaps to Henry and a Henry pass attempt, but it ultimately proved futile. Things appeared to be trending in the right direction as the Ravens played the Jaguars to a tightly contested game through the first 29 minutes before Parker Washington broke the game open with a 50-yard touchdown in the final minute before the break. Things got nasty for Henry after the half as he managed only two additional yards after bruising his way to 55 first half yards. Henry will return to RB1 status in fantasy circles in Week 10 when the Ravens take on the Chargers.

item.title: Justice Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding seven yards on three receptions.
item.description:
Justice Hill BAL Running Back

Hill became the first running back to amass more than 75 yards against the Jaguars since the start of the 2025 regular season with a 65-yard touchdown with the game well out of hand in the second half. It was an otherwise poor showing for the entirety of the Baltimore offense with a rookie undrafted free agent starting his first NFL game. Hill remains nothing more than a desperation FLEX ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Chargers.

item.title: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Shedeur Sanders will start in Week 9 against the Saints.
item.description:
Shedeur Sanders CLE Quarterback

Sanders will draw the start as Deshaun Watson (concussion) has yet to clear protocol in time to be ready for Sunday’s game. Interestingly, Watson is still expected to be listed as questionable, per Monken, but Sanders will draw the start. We are assuming this decision is based on Sanders taking first-team reps after Watson missed each of the first two days of practice, but this is a nice opportunity for Sanders to show whatever growth he has made since a tough rookie season in which he threw for 1,440 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions in eight games played. He’ll be on the low-end QB2 radar on the road against the Saints, who rank 16th in fantasy points allowed to opposing QBs this season.

Source: Andrew Siciliano

item.title: Hunter Henry (foot) has been ruled questionable for Week 9 against the Packers.
item.description:

The Patriots are down A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) on top of their other skill-position issues, so if Henry can go, he could see a considerable amount of targets against the Packers. He didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday, however, so it seems unlikely. Eli Raridon is inline to be the top tight end option if Henry can’t play.

item.title: Joe Fagnano completed 10-of-18 passes for 60 yards and two interceptions in the Ravens’ 33-10, Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding 13 yards on three carries.
item.description:
Joe Fagnano BAL Quarterback

Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did everything he could to scheme around a starting undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in his first NFL start, calling numerous exotic looks to include direct snaps to Derrick Henry, a Henry pass attempt, quick outs to Zay Flowers, Flowers rush attempts, and flea flickers, but it wasn’t enough to overcome poor execution, consistently off-target throws, and a lack of downfield ability. The Ravens also committed numerous pre-snap penalties as they continue to lead the league in that area through nine weeks, which killed multiple drives. Fagnano managed only 25 pass yards in the first half, finishing with a ridiculous 60 yards, while both interceptions came in the second half with the team in desperation mode. Fagnano leaves his first, and likely last, NFL start with a sour taste in his mouth, as he likely retreats to backup duties following the signing of veteran Jacoby Brissett earlier in the week.

item.title: Brenton Strange caught both targets for 22 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Brenton Strange

Strange was overshadowed by the 52-yard reception from fellow tight end Nate Boerkircher on the team’s opening possession, but he made a really nice grab in triple coverage over the middle of the field to set up the team’s second score of the game. Strange remains unlikely to see consistent volume for as long as the Jaguars continue to so handily control games, something that appears likely to continue given the team holds the weakest strength of schedule for the remainder of the regular season. Fantasy managers likely have better options ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

item.title: Parker Washington caught 2-of-7 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Parker Washington

Both of Washington’s receptions came before the break, the second of which was a 50-yard touchdown on a double-move slant against Cover-0 with under one minute remaining before the half. Washington remains one of the most efficient receivers in the league but consistently positive game scripts have left the overall pass volume lacking, particularly in the second half this season. He remains an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

item.title: Jakobi Meyers caught 4-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

All four of Meyers’ receptions came before the half in what remained a tighter game until just before the half, when alpha wide receiver Parker Washington took a simple slant for a 50-yard touchdown with under a minute remaining before the break. As has been the case on numerous occasions this season, Jacksonville coasted in the second half, limiting overall pass volume after the break. Meyers narrowly missed his first touchdown since Week 3 as he was tackled at the one on the team’s first possession. He remains a viable FLEX option ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

item.title: Chris Rodriguez rushed 10 times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
item.description:
Chris Rodriguez

Rodriguez split time with lead back Bhayshul Tuten in the first half before soaking up most of the backfield work in the third quarter. Both backs would then cede primary duties to special team ace Ameer Abdullah in the fourth quarter when the game was well in hand. Rodriguez has seen his fantasy value plummet of late with the emergence of Tuten as a borderline workhorse, a situation that was heavily influenced by Tuten’s lack of practice ahead of Thursday Night Football. The long week appears likely to provide the time needed for Tuten to return to full strength, leaving Rodriguez as a touchdown-dependent FLEX when the Jaguars face the Titans in Week 10.

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

Tuten started after failing to practice in any capacity this week, capping off the opening drive with a score from one yard out. He would split time with Chris Rodriguez for the rest of the first half before giving way to the combination of Rodriguez and special teams ace Ameer Abdullah for the bulk of the second half with the game in hand. Tuten should see his volume tick back up toward lead back territory when the Jaguars face off against the Titans in Week 10, where he will return to RB2 status.

item.title: Trevor Lawrence completed 16-of-26 passes for 242 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ 33-10, Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Trevor Lawrence

It was business as usual for Lawrence and the Jaguars, who won their eighth game by 20 or more points since the start of the 2025 season, the most in the league during that span. Lawrence looked sharp throughout, starting things off with a touchdown drive on their opening possession that was sparked by a 52-yard completion to tight end Nate Boerkircher. He would hit Parker Washington on a slant for a 50-yard touchdown in the final minute before the half to push the lead to 17-3, with a flurry of second half field goals enough to chase the reeling Ravens from the field. In standard Jacksonville fashion, positive game script capped Lawrence’s aerial volume, something fantasy managers have both gotten used to through the mid way point in the season and will likely see continue considering the Jaguars hold the league’s softest remaining strength of schedule. The win pushes the Jaguars to 6-2 and extends their lead in the AFC South ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the one-win Titans, where Lawrence will remain a back end QB1 due to lack of volume.

item.title: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that the Ravens are willing to make Lamar Jackson the highest-paid player in NFL history.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Well, that’s good, because it will assuredly take a record-setting deal to keep him in a Ravens uniform. Jackson has an $84.34 million salary cap hit next season, so the team has to do something with his contract. Jackson has a no-trade clause and a no-franchise tag clause — he possesses a ton of leverage. Per Palmer, the two sides will not negotiate a new deal in-season, so they will try to get something done between the end of the season and the beginning of free agency, which starts in March 2027.

Source: James Palmer

item.title: Michael Wilson (NIR-rest/ribs) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Michael Wilson ARI Wide Receiver

Wilson will face the Seahawks this weekend, barring a setback. It’s a tough matchup, but Wilson’s target volume keeps him worth of remaining in starting lineups. Wilson showed decent chemistry with Gardner Minshew last week, which was nice to see, now that Jacoby Brissett is headed to the Ravens.

Source: Arizona Cardinals

item.title: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

Shaheed seems likely to miss another week, though he could technically still turn things around tomorrow. Seahawks LT Charles Cross (ankle) also remains sidelined on Thursday, and LG Quenton Nelson (knee) was downgraded to a non-participant. Hopefully, Nelson’s absence is precautionary.

item.title: Drew Lock (elbow) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:

Lock has been dealing with an injury in his throwing arm since Week 7, but he told reporters that he is feeling good now. Lock played very well as Sam Darnold’s replacement earlier this year. As long as the elbow holds up, Lock should be expected to do so again. He is a viable QB2.

item.title: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

The Saints’ first-round rookie is now on the wrong side of questionable. It would have been nice to see him practice in full today. That said, New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill commented positively on Tyson’s performance, saying Tyson “does not look limited.”

Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

The way the team listed Kamara indicates that the back injury will not keep him from playing, but he is clearly still hurt. Kamara has been entirely ineffective this season and can only be viewed as a touchdown-dependent FLEX. CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was unable to practice today.

Source: New Orleans Saints

item.title: Myles Garrett (knee) limited again on Thursday.
item.description:
Myles Garrett

Garrett has a chance to face the Commanders this week, but he still belongs in the questionable column at this time. Rams CB1 Trent McDuffie (back) and S Kam Curl (foot) both missed practice for the second time this week.

Source: Ben Standig

item.title: Matthew Stafford (right elbow) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Matthew Stafford

Stafford has downplayed inquiries regarding his throwing-arm injury, saying he’s been icing his elbow post-game and post-practice for a while now — and he called out the beat reporters for missing it. Lingering elbow soreness isn’t exactly reassuring, but at least he is practicing fully. Stafford should be good to go for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders, but this is obviously worth monitoring.

item.title: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.

David Njoku LAC Tight End

item.title: Travon Walker (ribs) is active for Week 9 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Travon Walker

The Jaguars’ No. 2 edge rusher will play through his ribs injury tonight. He apparently got hurt during Tuesday’s practice, but is good to go two days later. The Jaguars declared WR CJ Williams, CB Alijah Huzzie, S Cam’Ron Silmon-Craig and DE Wesley Williams inactive for Week 9 against the Ravens.

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the Eagles have received “a ton of interest” on the trade market for Moro Ojomo.

Moro Ojomo PHI Defensive Tackle

With both Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis signed for multiple seasons, investing heavily in another defensive tackle might be cost-prohibitive. Perhaps the Eagles are simply trying to drive up Ojomo’s trade value. Stay tuned.

Breer believes a fourth-round pick “seems like a lot” to give up for an aging running back who is set to enter free agency at the end of the year. So, Pollard might end up staying in Tennessee. Bhayshul Tuten

Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Nabers worked with trainers today instead of practicing with his teammates. He told reporters after practicing that he is “good” to go for Week 9 against the Eagles. We believe him. The Giants have managed his reps at times during the practice week this year.

Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

The Ravens’ rookie running back will have to wait to make his debut. The Ravens declared QB Kedon Slovis, WR Elijah Sarratt, OL Emery Jones Jr., DL Aeneas Peebles, CB Nate Wiggins and S Jaylinn Hawkins inactive. Hawkins is dealing with a knee injury and Wiggins, the Ravens’ No. 1 cornerback, is listed with a stinger and an illness. Slovis will serve as the emergency third quarterback. Austin Reed is the QB2. Ravens RG Vega Ioane (knee) will play.

item.description:
Christian Darrisaw MIN Tackle

item.description:
Jauan Jennings MIN Wide Receiver

Source: Minnesota Vikings

item.title: Dion Dawkins (ribs) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Dion Dawkins BUF Tackle

Dawkins, the Bills’ left tackle, and LG Alec Anderson (ankle) were both absent today. They have an extra day to rest, since the Bills face the Vikings in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game. Hopefully, the extra time allows them to suit up against Minnesota’s elite defense.

Source: Buffalo Bills PR

item.title: Keon Coleman (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Keon Coleman BUF Wide Receiver

Coleman was seen wearing a red non-contact jersey at today’s practice. His limited session to begin the week puts him on track to face the Vikings in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game. With DJ Moore (shoulder) back in the lineup, Coleman is just a WR4/FLEX. Joshua Palmer (hamstring) did not practice.

Source: Buffalo Bills PR

item.title: Dalton Kincaid (chest) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Kincaid should be good to go for the Bills’ Monday Night Football game against the Vikings. It’s a tough matchup, and he could be asked to block more than usual. Still, Kincaid warrants TE1 treatment thanks to his talent, usage and quarterback.

Source: Buffalo Bills PR

item.title: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

There was some concern that Moore may have injured his knee in Week 8 against the Ravens, but he is listed only with the same shoulder issue he has dealt with for weeks, which is good news. Moore should be treated as a WR2 in a very tough matchup against the Vikings on Monday Night Football.

Source: Buffalo Bills PR

item.title: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Talanoa Hufanga DEN Safety

The Broncos’ safety now has a chance to play in Week 9 against the Panthers, though it is possible he still needs another week. Getting Hufanga back in the lineup will help improve a Broncos defense that has somewhat underperformed this year.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Rashee Rice KC Wide Receiver

Rice is on track to face the Jets this weekend, as expected. The Chiefs’ embattled wide receiver also reportedly filed for bankruptcy this week, theoretically adding extra incentive to play well enough for a decent contract when he enters free agency next offseason. Rice is a fantasy football WR2.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Travis Kelce (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Travis Kelce KC Tight End

This time last week, Kelce was still a limited participant. Today’s upgraded status is a good sign for his overall health. The Chiefs’ stalwart tight end earned eight targets last week despite the ailment. He can be treated as a fantasy football TE1 against the Jets this week.

Source: Pete Sweeney

item.title: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was spotted at practice Thursday.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson had his 21-day practice window open up, and it’s a positive sign that he’s been able to practice on back-to-back days. There’s no guarantee he’ll play in Week 9 against the Commanders, but even if he misses that contest, it seems likely the second-year tight end will be back for the second half of the campaign.

Source: Sarah Barshop

item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

This makes two straight missed practices for Ferguson because of his ankle injury suffered in Week 8 versus the Cardinals. At this point, it seems unlikely that he’ll be able to play in Week 9 against the Colts, and there are better fantasy options even if he were to be able to go.

Source: Nick Harris

item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

Tuten did not practice at all this week, though the Jaguars notably kept many injured players limited, so it is possible that his absences were mostly precautionary. Tuten injured his ankle and foot in Week 8 against the Colts, but still managed to total 159 scrimmage yards, two catches and two touchdowns. He is an RB1 if active.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: George Pickens (hamstring) was limited during Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Pickens was also limited during Wednesday’s session. The 25-year-old still seems to be on target to play in Week 9 against the Colts, but fantasy managers would obviously like to see Pickens get in a full session before that contest.

Source: Nick Harris

Myles Garrett

Source: Sarah Barshop

item.title: Hunter Henry (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Hunter Henry NE Tight End

It’s looking like rookie Eli Raridon will operate as the Patriots’ No. 1 tight end in Week 9 against the Packers. Henry has not participated in football activities since injuring his foot early in Week 8 against the Dolphins. Raridon would warrant streaming TE1 consideration if he gets the start.

Source: New England Patriots

item.title: Mack Hollins (calf) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Mack Hollins NE Wide Receiver

Hollins is firmly in the questionable column with one practice left in Week 9. If active, he would be a boom-bust FLEX. The Patriots’ healthy wide receivers have played well in Hollins’ absence, though the team would probably like to get their field-stretcher back in action before long.

Source: New England Patriots

item.title: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Brown seems highly unlikely to play in Week 9 against the Packers. The Patriots could shut him down for a little while, with the goal of getting his degenerative knee and early-season high-ankle sprain healed. For now, fantasy managers should make backup plans in the short term.

Source: New England Patriots

item.title: MarShawn Lloyd was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday’s practice due to a knee injury.
item.description:
MarShawn Lloyd GB Running Back

Lloyd was good to go for Wednesday’s session, so this appears to be a new issue. Chris Brooks was also limited by his ankle injury for a second-straight practice. Lloyd and Brooks — if healthy — will be the backups to Josh Jacobs for Week 9, and don’t offer much fantasy upside, if any.

Source: Rob Demovsky

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Christian Watson (rib) was limited during Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Christian Watson GB Wide Receiver

It’s back-to-back limited sessions for Watson. It’ll likely be a pain-tolerance issue for the wideout, but assuming he doesn’t suffer a setback in practice, he appears to be good for Week 9 against the Patriots and deserves WR1 consideration.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Denzel Boston (calf) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

Boston is on track to face the Saints this week, but lower-body injuries have limited his production since Week 4. The Browns are also likely to have Shedeur Sanders under center, adding an unknown variable to the mix as the two players hone their chemistry. Boston is likely just a boom-bust FLEX.

Source: Mary Kay Cabot

item.title: Tristan Wirfs (toe) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Tristan Wirfs TB Tackle

It’s a new injury designation for Wirfs, so it seems likely that the ailment occurred during Wednesday’s practice. The Buccaneers already have offensive line issues, and anyone who saw the Bears ravage the Seahawks’ offensive line knows what that unit is capable of. It could be a long day for Baker Mayfield if Wirfs can’t go.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Kenny Gainwell was a full participant in Thursday’s practice.
item.description:
Kenny Gainwell TB Running Back

Gainwell never seemed in danger of missing Week 9 against the Bears, but the 27-year-old should be just fine for the Week 9 bout against the Bears. He’s coming off a monster 140-yard performance against Atlanta, but keep in mind that Tampa Bay was basically a service academy school for that game with zero completions. He’s closer to FLEX than RB2.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

After only participating in drills on the side and being listed as a non-participant Wednesday, Egbuka was a full-go for Thursday’s session. The 24-year-old will likely need to get in one more full session before fantasy managers can fully trust the wideout for Week 9 against the Bears, but this is obviously a significant step in the right direction.

Source: Adam Caplan
